title: Still Learning Love
north_star: A soft illustrated archive of Aachu and Zuv's love, chaos, culture, and tiny rituals.

golden_theme_contract.first_principles_rule: Before submitting or scoring any new carousel idea, use these source files as the first-principles explanation of why the gold carousel worked: universal anti-ideal -> concrete Aachu proof -> Zuv steady response -> tender acceptance thesis.
golden_theme_contract.rule: Every carousel must start from a universal relationship truth, then prove it through Aachu/Zuv specifics. Photos, places, outfits, and objects are evidence, not the premise.
hard_fail_if: The concept is primarily about an object, outfit, location, or photo aesthetic.
A stranger could not send the carousel to a partner without knowing the private photo context.
Aachu's expressive role is missing or mocked.
Zuv's calm role is passive, absent, or treated as background.
The concept is mostly about taking photos, looking beautiful, glowing, or waiting for one more picture without a deeper relationship tension.
One partner's role is only looking good while the other waits or holds things.
The final thesis is generic romance without a concrete proof trail.
default_five_slide_map: Universal hook: one swipe-stopping relationship truth.
Aachu-specific reveal: her version of the truth.
Concrete proof: a drawable behavior, object, or ritual from the reference material.
Zuv role: what his calm, patience, care, or choice does emotionally.
Save/share thesis: the tender truth underneath the joke.
caption_formula: Open with the universal relationship truth.
Show the couple-specific behavior, care, posture, object, or rhythm in the middle; name Aachu/Zuv only when natural.
End with a soft send/save-worthy thesis.

successful_carousel_standard.rule: Build a public identity mirror with concrete couple receipts, active Zuv care, an emotional reversal, and a send/save thesis; stage the story in visible actions before choosing poster text; do not optimize for keywords.
successful_carousel_standard.open_reasoning_policy: Expose the real goal and selection logic; do not optimize for keywords or let slide copy substitute for staged story action.
successful_carousel_standard.prompt_rule: Prompts must prove relationship behavior through stage-scene Aachu/Zuv action; text completes the scene instead of carrying it.

human_truth: Healthy love is not being contradiction-free; it is noticing sooner and returning softer.
emotional_arc: ideal -> small contradiction -> visible repair -> softer return
source_story_summary: Aachu and Zuv believe in healthy love, but one ordinary fight shows they are still learning it. A cup lands too firmly on the kitchen counter before patience arrives. At the table, one listens while also preparing a reply. One asks for space, but the bedroom door stays half open. The apology does not come as a speech; it comes as a warm cup of tea placed beside a quiet hand. Later that night, they do not solve forever, they only repair today. By morning, the door is open, the cups are together, and they choose softness sooner than last time.
visual_style: Reference typography lock: use the same rounded, imperfect, airy handwritten lowercase font style as the supplied screenshots; warm white lettering on dark scenes, warm charcoal on light scenes; no platform UI, carousel dots, arrows, social handles, quote-card overlays, or book promo copy. Keep @a.storyof.two house watercolor-and-ink style and exact integrated on-image text. Typography override from supplied screenshots: rounded, imperfect, airy handwritten lowercase; uneven human spacing; warm white ink on dark scenes and warm charcoal on light scenes; integrated into the artwork, never UI or quote-card type.
target_voice: Aachu/Zuv archive voice: warm, specific, playful underneath the tenderness

story_selling_contract.rule: Begin concept thinking like an author: find the relationship obstacle, choose one process card, prove the feeling with Aachu/Zuv behavior, then score before writing slides or captions.

human_story_setup.visible_human_proof: Seven concrete receipts: mid-fight distance, too-firm cup, waiting-to-reply posture, half-open door, tea apology, late-night repair, morning softness.
human_story_setup.active_partner_role: Zuv is not a rescuer; he participates in the mutual repair through the half-open door, the tea/apology beat, and the quieter morning return.

human_story_setup.earned_payoff: Maybe love is noticing the pattern, and choosing softness sooner.

success_definition.audience_success: A cold viewer recognizes a real post-fight repair pattern and sends it to their partner.
success_definition.creative_success: The deck proves self-awareness through staged couple behavior, not self-help advice.
success_definition.brand_success: The idea feels like @a.storyof.two because it turns a small home repair ritual into a soft love thesis.
success_definition.production_success: The route can become native 3:4 and separate 9:16 identity-referenced illustrations with exact handwritten text.
success_definition.story_theme_success: Protect the reference's human contradiction theme while making it couple-specific and visually staged.

stage_scene_gate.action: The couple moves through a small fight: distance, a too-firm cup, listening poorly, asking for space, offering tea, repairing at night, returning softer in the morning.
stage_scene_gate.reaction: Each slide shows the body reacting before the moral arrives: still-angled feet, frozen hands, held breath, half-open door, lowered eyes, tired closeness, morning touch.
stage_scene_gate.eye_line_or_attention: Eye-lines shift from avoidance to partial attention to direct soft return by the final slide.
stage_scene_gate.hands_or_object_movement: Cup set down, napkin/phone gripped, door left ajar, tea placed beside a hand, blanket or shared mess repaired, two cups together by morning.
stage_scene_gate.silence_or_pause: The strongest beats are pauses: after the fight, before the reply, behind the half-open door, and before accepting the tea.
stage_scene_gate.consequence: Sendable to a partner as a gentle 'this is us when we are trying' mirror, especially after small fights or apology moments.
stage_scene_gate.reversal_or_payoff: The carousel moves from confession of imperfection to proof that awareness can become tenderness in the very next ordinary action.

slides.copy:
we talk about healthy love,
but we still learn it mid-fight.
slides.visual: Immediate cover contradiction: Aachu and Zuv are mid-fight in a lived-in room, verbally tense but not cruel. Their bodies are angled away, hands animated, brows tight, with tiny signs they still care: one cup between them, a blanket half-shared, feet still pointed toward each other. Make it active, not quiet poster sadness.
slides.job: Stop the scroll with the honest contradiction and make the fight theme immediately legible.

slides.copy:
we talk about patience,
but sometimes our tone arrives first.
slides.visual: Show the two verbally fighting or sharply talking over each other in a kitchen or small room. One partner points or lifts a hand mid-sentence while the other reacts, a cup/spoon/object landing too hard on the counter. The receipt is tone arriving before patience: visible mouths open, tense hands, not physical aggression.
slides.job: Stage the first specific verbal-fight behavior that proves the contradiction.

slides.copy:
we talk about listening,
but sometimes we just don't listen at all.
slides.visual: Stage a clear not-listening beat: both partners are in the same room but mentally elsewhere, one talking while the other looks away at a phone, cupboard, or floor; or both speak at once with crossed eye-lines. It should feel instantly recognizable: they are hearing sound, not receiving each other.
slides.job: Make viewers recognize how not-listening looks inside a relationship.

slides.copy:
we talk about giving space,
but still always irritate the hell out of each other.
slides.visual: Action over words: one partner tries to get space on a bed, sofa, or floor corner, while the other keeps hovering nearby and irritating them in a petty familiar way: poking, making faces, moving a pillow, tapping the door, or standing too close. Make it funny-irritating, not mean.
slides.job: Carry the truth through familiar irritation and failed space.

slides.copy:
we talk about saying sorry,
but never apologies when we should.
slides.visual: Show the apology failure actively: both partners are close enough to repair but stubbornly not apologizing. One holds a cup or folded arms; the other looks away with a wounded-but-proud face. The apology is available in the room but withheld. No peaceful tea apology; this beat is the stubborn silence after the fight.
slides.job: Repeat the contradiction through the stubborn apology gap.

slides.copy:
we talk about forever,
but we fight like we don't know each other.
slides.visual: The strongest fight receipt: late evening, both tired and emotional, standing/sitting apart like strangers in their own room. Their posture says they know each other deeply, but the fight has made them act unfamiliar. Use distance, crossed eye-lines, scattered blanket/cups, and one small shared object between them.
slides.job: Sharpen the reversal: forever-talk versus stranger-like fighting.

slides.copy:
maybe love is noticing the pattern,
and choosing softness sooner.
slides.visual: Morning-after or after-fight payoff: the fight energy softens through action, not a grand hug. One partner reaches first, adjusts a blanket, moves closer, or offers a small touch; the other accepts. The room still has traces of the fight, but the body language shows they noticed the pattern sooner.
slides.job: Land the saveable lesson through a visible choice toward softness.
